 JUDGMENT This petition is filed by the petitioner against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:
On 22.02.2024 at about 04.30 p.m, while the petitioner was riding his Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-06-HL-4608 near Bidanagere Cross, Tavarekere - Ballagere Road,
Hebbur Hobli, Tumkuru Taluk, at that time the rider of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-64-L-3485 rode the same at very high speed, in (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.1806/2024 rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's Motor Cycle from opposite direction.
Due to which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Hemavathi hospital, Tumkuru, for treatment.
The petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses.

Prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 38 years and was doing Mango business and earning Rs.35,000/- p.m. Due to accidental injuries, he is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest, as such incurring loss of income and suffered permanent disability.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending Motor Cycle involved in the accident and in this regard the Hebbur Police have registered a case against rider of the said offending Motor Cycle.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the R.C Owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending offending Motor Cycle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and have filed written statement.

Respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, avocation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and stated that this respondent had valid driving licence at the time of accident and also insurance is in force from 24.01.2024 to 23.01.2025 and if the petitioner is entitled for compensation, only the respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation and pray for dismiss the petition against respondent No.1.
05.

The respondent No.2 in its written statement denied the entire case of the petitioner and admits that this respondent has issued the policy bearing No.2301206052015200000 against the Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-64-L-3485, valid from 24.01.2024 to 23.01.2025 and the liability of this Maniunvar Pasha Allias Munwar Pasha ... vs Meharaj on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60332692/
2 respondent, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

sentences.text:
It is further denied age, avocation,
income of the petitioner, manner of accident, negligence of the rider of the Motor Cycle and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.1806/2024 and expenses incurred by the petitioner and contended that the petitioner has not come before this Court with clean hands and a false complaint has been lodged against the insured vehicle after thought by twisting the facts and colluding concerned persons in order to get compensation and situation of the alleged accident

has been twisted and described as if the insured vehicle is involved and responsible for the alleged accident and the stated facts are far from truth and the petitioner was riding his Motor Cycle without knowledge of riding, without wearing helmet and without possessing valid vehicle documents in a rash and negligent manner and he had suffered self accident and the respondent No.1 was knowingly riding the insured vehicle without possessing valid and effective driving licence and therefore, he has consciously breached the terms and conditions of the policy and absolved this respondent from indemnifying the liability, if any, under the alleged cause of action and the compensation claimed is highly exaggerated and hence, pray to dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
06.

On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following Issues:-
 (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.1806/2024  ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 22.02.2024 at about 4.30 p.m, near Bidanagere Cross, Tavarekere, Ballagere Road, Tumkur, due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-64-L-3485 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03. What Order or Award?

07. The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and got examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and through them got marked 19 documents as Ex.P.1 to 19 and closed the petitioner side evidence.

Despite sufficient opportunity, the respondents did not lead evidence,
hence, respondents evidence is taken as nil.
08. The learned counsels for the petitioner and respondents have argued on main matter and perused the records.

09. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.1806/2024  Issue No.1 In the Affirmative  Issue No.2
Partly in the affirmative Maniunvar Pasha Allias Munwar Pasha ... vs Meharaj

As per final order  for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.
Though he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing has been brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that he lodged complaint after 2 days of accident and his Motor Cycle front portion was damaged and denied to the suggestion that on the date of accident he rode his Motor Cycle in rash and negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle and fell down and sustained injuries and offending Motor Cycle has not caused any accident and admits that he has not produced any document to show he was earning Rs.35,000/- p.m.

Further, PW.2 is a Doctor, who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability of the petitioner, has stated that the petitioner sustained T12 and L1 vertebral compression fracture and he assessed permanent physical disability of 30% of spine which is 15% of whole body and he further stated that petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implant and he has produced Outpatient book and X-ray as per Ex.P.14 and 15.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that he has not personally treated the petitioner and has not seen old X-ray, OPD records and Case sheet and admits that if the injured has taken follow-up treatment, then same is recorded in OPD book.

If the injured has taken follow-up treatment regularly, then there may be chances of reducing disability and also admits that as per Discharge summary, condition of the petitioner is stable and that there is improvement in the condition of the petitioner, fractures are stabilize and he has assessed only physical disability and denied to the suggestion that permanent disability can be assessed only after removal of implants and he has not issued any estimation regarding future surgery and he has not issued any disability certificate.

Further, the Manager in Medical Record Department at Hemavathi hospital, Tumkuru, is examined as PW.3 and he has produced Authorization letter, Case sheet, X-ray and MRI scan films as per Ex.P.16 to 19.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that doctor who treated the petitioner is still working in their hospital and he does not know the nature of treatment given to the petitioner and he does now know the contents of documents produced by him.
13. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked 19 documents as Ex.P.1 to 19 on his behalf.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Hebbur Police against the rider of the offending Motor Cycle for his rash and negligent riding and caused the accident.
Ex.P.2 is copy of Complaint.

Ex.P.5 is copy of Wound certificate which shows the petitioner has sustained one grievous injury in the road traffic accident.

Ex.P.6 is copy of Charge Sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against rider/respondent No.1 of offending Motor Cycle for rash and negligent riding and (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.1806/2024 causing accident and grievous injuries to the petitioner.
Ex.P.8 is Discharge summary, which discloses that petitioner was admitted to Hemavathi hospital as inpatient on 22.02.2024 and discharged on 05.03.2024 for 12 days due to accidental injuries.
Ex.P.11 is MRI, CT and Ultra sound reports.
Ex.P.12 is X-ray.
Ex.P.13 is CT scan films.
Ex.P.14 is Outpatient book.
Ex.P.15 is X-ray.
Ex.P.17 is Case sheet.
Ex.P.18 is X-ray and Ex.P.19 is MRI scan films.

14. On going through the oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner, the petitioner has clearly established and proved that the he sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 22.02.2024 at about 04.30 p.m, near Bidanagere Cross, Tavarekere - Ballagere Road, Hebbur Hobli, Tumkuru Taluk, due to rash and negligent act of riding of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-64-L-3485 by its rider, as alleged in the petition.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.1806/2024 and was aged about 38 years and was doing Mango business and earning Rs.35,000/- p.m and has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
Due to accidental injuries, he has undergone pain and sufferings, loss of income, unable to do work and became permanent disabled.
16. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced copy of Driving licence at Ex.P.7.

Eventhough the said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence regarding his exact date of birth, the said document can be relied upon and according to which his date of birth is mentioned as 15.06.1976 and the alleged accident occurred on 22.04.2024 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner is 48 years

. Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 48 years and as per the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and Others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 46 to 50 is 13.

sentences.text: So far as avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, the petitioner has not placed any documents or evidence before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the Maniunvar Pasha Allias Munwar Pasha ... vs Meharaj on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60332692/

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.16,500/-.

18 . According to the evidence of PW.2, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner has sustained T12 and L1 vertebral compression fracture and he assessed permanent physical disability of 30% of spine which is 15% of whole body.
However, considering the evidence of PW.2 and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 10%.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:-
As per Ex.P.8 Discharge summary the petitioner was admitted to Hemavathi (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.1806/2024 hospital as inpatient for 12 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.

Therefore,
considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

20. Pain and sufferings:- As per Ex.P.5 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 doctor and as per Ex.P.11 MRI, CT and Ultra sound reports, Ex.P.12 X-ray, Ex.P.13 CT scan films, Ex.P.14 Outpatient book Ex.P.15 X-ray, Ex.P.17 Case sheet, Ex.P.18 X-ray and Ex.P.19 MRI Scan films and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner would have undergone pain and agony.
Accordingly with regard to fracture suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
21. Loss of income during laid up period:-

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.16,500/- p.m and he was admitted in the hospital for 12 days as inpatient.

Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.1806/2024 not have carried out his avocation for atleast two months.
Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.33,000/- (Rs.16,500 x 2) under this head.
22. Medical expenses:-
As per Ex.P.9 Medical bills, the petitioner has incurred total medical expenses of Rs.1,76,602/-.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,76,602/- under this head.

23. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
24. Future medical expenses:-

The PW.2 doctor has stated in his chief-examination that petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implant, but he has not stated the actual cost and has not Maniunvar Pasha Allias Munwar Pasha ... vs Meharaj

6 produced any estimation regarding future medical expenses.
Hence, this tribunal has awarded sum of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
25. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

(SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.1806/2024 Sl. Head of Compensation Amount No. in Rs.
 1. Loss of future income 2,57,400-00  2. Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00

3 . Attendant charges, extra 30,000-00  nutritious food and  conveyance charges  4. Medical Expenses 1,76,602-00  5. Loss of future amenities and 30,000-00  unhappiness  6. Loss of income during laid up 33,000-00  period
7. Future medical expenses 30,000-00  Total 5,87,002-00 26.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,87,002/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.

27. Regarding liability:- Though the respondents have appeaed before the tribunal and filed their written statements and contested the matter, but they have not lead their evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner and prove their defence.

28. The respondent No.2 Insurance Company in his written statement at para 2 admits that this (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.1806/2024 respondent has issued policy bearing No.23012060520 15200000 against the Motor Cycle bearing No. KA-64-L-3485, valid from 24.01.2024 to 23.01.2025 and the alleged accident occurred on 22.02.2024.
Therefore, it appears that as on the date of accident the policy of the offending vehicle is valid and is in force.
Hence, the respondent No.1 being the R.C Owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Motor Cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since policy of offending Motor Cycle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall deposit compensation amount of Rs.5,87,002/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
29. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
